title_en: Interpretation of the Supreme People's Court on Issues concerning the Application of Law in the Trial of Cases of Execution Objection Lawsuits

articles.content_en:
Article 1 If a person other than a party raises an enforcement objection against the subject matter of enforcement during the enforcement process pursuant to Article 238 of the Civil Procedure Law, the people's court responsible for enforcing the subject matter of enforcement at the time the objection is raised shall review and handle the objection; where the person other than a party or a party is dissatisfied with the ruling on the enforcement objection and files an enforcement objection lawsuit with the enforcement court that made the ruling within 15 days from the date of service of the ruling, the people's court shall accept the case.
If the person other than a party fails to raise an objection within the time limit specified in Article 6 of the Provisions of the Supreme People's Court on Several Issues concerning the Handling of Cases of Objection and Reconsideration in Enforcement by People's Courts, and the people's court rules not to accept the case, the person other than a party may separately assert rights against the enforcement applicant, the person subject to enforcement, or others according to law.

Article 2 During property preservation or enforcement in a dispute over a monetary claim, if the subject matter of enforcement is subject to successive seizures, impoundments, or freezings, the person other than a party filing an enforcement objection lawsuit shall name as defendants the preservation applicant or enforcement applicant who first conducted the seizure or who enjoys priority rights to satisfaction such as security interests, and name as third parties other known preservation applicants or enforcement applicants who have conducted successive seizures.

Article 3 Where a person other than a party enjoys a civil right or interest sufficient to exclude compulsory enforcement over the subject matter of enforcement, and the people's court renders a judgment that the subject matter of enforcement shall not be enforced, it shall at the same time render a judgment to lift the enforcement measures and specify the case number of the relevant seizure, impoundment, or freezing order. The person other than a party may request the relevant enforcement court to lift the enforcement measures by producing the effective judgment.

Article 4 Where a person other than a party files an enforcement objection lawsuit and makes a request for confirmation of rights over the attribution of the subject matter of enforcement in accordance with Article 234 of the Civil Code or other provisions, the person subject to enforcement shall be named as the defendant.

Article 5 Where a person other than a party files an enforcement objection lawsuit and makes a claim for performance, such as returning the original property, returning the price, delivering the subject matter, or going through the formalities of transfer registration, against the person subject to enforcement or others as defendants, the people's court may hear the cases in a consolidated manner; if the law otherwise provides that consolidated hearing is inappropriate, separate case filings shall be conducted.

Article 7 During the trial of an enforcement objection lawsuit or the review of an application for retrial filed by a person other than a party, if the enforcement case has been closed, the enforcement court has not disposed of the subject matter of enforcement, and the enforcement measures have been lifted, the people's court shall rule to terminate the lawsuit or terminate the review. The original enforcement objection ruling made by the enforcement court shall cease to have effect. For the requests for confirmation of rights or performance made by the person other than a party pursuant to Articles 4 and 5 of this Interpretation, the people's court may continue the trial or review.

Article 8 During the trial of an enforcement objection lawsuit or the review of an application for retrial, if the people's court decides to conduct a retrial according to law of the original judgment, ruling, or other documents that serve as the basis for enforcement, and the subject matter of enforcement is property other than the subject matter of dispute involved in the original judgment, ruling, or other documents, or the person other than a party may enjoy a civil right or interest sufficient to exclude compulsory enforcement such as priority rights to satisfaction (including security interests), the enforcement objection lawsuit may continue to be tried or reviewed; if it cannot be determined that the person other than a party enjoys a civil right or interest sufficient to exclude compulsory enforcement, the enforcement objection lawsuit shall be suspended in trial or review.

Article 9 During the trial of an enforcement objection lawsuit or the review of an application for retrial, if the people's court rules to accept the bankruptcy case of the person subject to enforcement, the enforcement objection lawsuit shall be suspended in trial or review; after the administrator takes over the debtor's property, the enforcement objection lawsuit may resume trial or review.

Article 10 If, through the trial supervision procedure, it is discovered that the decision to support the person other than a party in excluding compulsory enforcement in an enforcement objection lawsuit is indeed erroneous, and the people's court determines that the person other than a party does not enjoy a civil right or interest sufficient to exclude compulsory enforcement and renders a judgment dismissing the claim of the person other than a party, the original relevant enforcement court shall resume enforcement in accordance with the original priority order; if the subject matter of enforcement has been lawfully transferred to another person and the people's court rules to revoke the original judgment and terminate the lawsuit, the enforcement applicant may separately assert rights against the person subject to enforcement, the person other than a party, or others according to law.

Article 12 Where an enforcement court freezes the supervision account for pre-sale funds of a real estate development enterprise subject to enforcement, and a person other than a party, on the ground that he or she has paid the purchase price into that account and that the housing sales contract has been rescinded, files an enforcement objection lawsuit requesting to exclude compulsory enforcement on the corresponding purchase price and to have it distributed to him or her, if the cause is established, the people's court shall support the claim.
Where an enforcement court carries out compulsory enforcement on the buildings of a real estate development enterprise subject to enforcement and the construction land-use right within the occupied area, and a consumer of commercial housing who meets the conditions specified in items (1) and (3) of the first paragraph of the preceding article, due to the non-delivery of the housing and the fact that actual delivery is unlikely, which may have led to the rescission of the housing sales contract, files an enforcement objection lawsuit requesting to exclude the corresponding compulsory enforcement from the conversion proceeds of the buildings and the construction land-use right and to have such proceeds distributed to him or her, the people's court shall support the claim.

Article 13 Where a people's court carries out compulsory enforcement on immovable property registered under the name of the person subject to enforcement, and a person other than a party, on the ground that he or she is the purchaser of the immovable property, files an enforcement objection lawsuit requesting to exclude compulsory enforcement of the priority right of construction project price payment, mortgage, and ordinary monetary claims, if the person other than a party has signed a lawful and valid written sales contract with the person subject to enforcement and the price delivered to the enforcement court before the conclusion of the court debate at first instance is sufficient to repay the corresponding principal claim on behalf of the person subject to enforcement, the people's court shall support the claim.
If a person other than a party who meets the conditions specified in the preceding paragraph files a lawsuit requesting the mortgagee to go through the formalities for cancellation of the mortgage registration on a per-unit basis, the people's court shall support the request.
If the people's court, in accordance with the first paragraph of this Article, renders a judgment that enforcement shall not be carried out, the enforcement applicant may apply to have the price delivered by the person other than a party pursuant to the first paragraph of this Article used to repay the corresponding debts of the person subject to enforcement.
If the people's court renders a judgment dismissing the claim of the person other than a party, the price delivered by the person other than a party for enforcement shall be promptly refunded.

Article 17 Where a people's court carries out compulsory enforcement on immovable property registered under the name of the employer (contracting party) subject to enforcement, and a person other than a party, on the ground that he or she has agreed with the person subject to enforcement to offset the project debt with the immovable property, files an enforcement objection lawsuit requesting to exclude compulsory enforcement of mortgage and ordinary monetary claims, and can prove that his or her claim simultaneously meets the following conditions, the people's court shall support the claim:
(1) Before the seizure, the person other than a party exercised the priority right of construction project price payment in accordance with Article 807 of the Civil Code and signed a lawful and valid agreement with the employer subject to enforcement to offset the debt through a price reduction (conversion) using the immovable property;
(2) Evidence shows that the amount of the debt offset is essentially equivalent to the actual value of the subject matter of enforcement at the time of the offset.
If the person other than a party files a lawsuit requesting the person subject to enforcement to go through the formalities for the transfer registration of ownership of the immovable property, and the conditions specified in the preceding paragraph are met, the people's court shall support the request according to law.

Article 18 Where a people's court carries out compulsory enforcement on immovable property registered under the name of the person subject to enforcement, and a person other than a party, on the ground that the immovable property is used for expropriation compensation in the form of property rights exchange, files an enforcement objection lawsuit requesting to exclude compulsory enforcement of the priority right of construction project price payment, mortgage, and other claims, and can prove that his or her claim simultaneously meets the following conditions, the people's court shall support the claim:
(1) Before the seizure, the person other than a party had signed an agreement of an expropriation compensation nature with the housing expropriation department, the housing expropriation implementation unit, or others according to law;
(2) The location of the immovable property used for expropriation compensation is clearly specified.
If the person other than a party files a lawsuit requesting the person subject to enforcement to go through the formalities for the transfer registration of ownership of the immovable property, and the conditions specified in the preceding paragraph are met, the people's court shall support the request according to law.

Article 19 Where a people's court carries out compulsory enforcement on immovable property registered under the name of the person subject to enforcement, and a person other than a party, on the ground that before the seizure he or she had signed a lawful and valid written sales contract with the person subject to enforcement, had paid the price in accordance with the contract, and had completed a lawful and valid advance notice registration for the immovable property, files an enforcement objection lawsuit requesting to cease disposition, if the cause is established, the people's court shall support the claim; if the conditions for real right registration are met and the person other than a party requests exclusion of compulsory enforcement, the people's court shall support the claim.

Article 20 In the case of compulsory enforcement without lease conducted through auction, sale by conversion, or other means, if a person other than a party, on the ground that before the seizure he or she had signed a lawful and valid written lease contract with the person subject to enforcement, had lawfully occupied and used the subject matter of enforcement, and had paid the rent in accordance with the contract, files an enforcement objection lawsuit requesting to exclude compulsory enforcement of ordinary claims without lease during the lease term, if the cause is established, the people's court shall support the claim; if the person other than a party who meets the conditions specified above signed the lease contract and lawfully occupied and used the subject matter of enforcement before the creation of the mortgage, and requests to exclude compulsory enforcement of the mortgage without lease during the lease term, the people's court shall support the claim.
The enforcement applicant may file a written objection against compulsory enforcement with lease conducted through auction, sale by conversion, or other means. After the enforcement court makes an enforcement ruling, if the person other than a party is dissatisfied and files a lawsuit with the enforcement court within 15 days from the date of service of the ruling, the matter shall be handled in accordance with the provisions of the preceding paragraph.
If the enforcement applicant is dissatisfied with the enforcement ruling, he or she may, within 15 days from the date of service of the ruling, file a lawsuit with the enforcement court naming the lessee and the person subject to enforcement as defendants, requesting compulsory enforcement of the subject matter of enforcement without lease. After trial, the people's court shall handle the matter separately according to the following circumstances:
(1) If the lessee meets the conditions specified in the first paragraph of this Article, the claim shall be dismissed by judgment;
(2) If the lessee does not meet the conditions specified in the first paragraph of this Article, the judgment shall permit compulsory enforcement of the subject matter of enforcement without lease.

Article 21 If a person other than a party colludes maliciously with the person subject to enforcement or the enforcement applicant, by forging evidence or unilaterally fabricating basic case facts, to hinder lawful enforcement through an enforcement objection lawsuit, the people's court shall dismiss his or her claim and impose a fine or detention depending on the severity of the circumstances; if the conduct is suspected of constituting a crime, the people's court shall transfer the criminal clues to the public security organ.
Litigation agents, witnesses, expert evaluation personnel, and other litigation participants shall be subject to the provisions of the preceding paragraph.
If a person other than a party or others causes the subject matter of enforcement to be unenforceable or to suffer diminution in value, thereby causing losses to the enforcement applicant, through fraudulent litigation or other means, he or she shall make compensation according to law.

Article 22 If an enforcement applicant files an enforcement objection lawsuit pursuant to Article 238 of the Civil Procedure Law, the relevant provisions of this Interpretation shall be applied mutatis mutandis.
Article 23 This Interpretation shall come into force as of July 24, 2025.
